summary: A conference organizer used an AI image-expansion tool to make a speaker's photo taller for an ad. The tool invented the lower part of the image, making the speaker's blouse appear unbuttoned with a hint of underwear. The organizers apologized and removed the content.
technical_summary: A generative outpainting feature extended a cropped portrait to a vertical format and fabricated new content, adding a sexualized detail the original photo lacked. The model's output reflected sexualized stereotypes of women's clothing. No human review caught it before the ad was posted.

summary: A class-action lawsuit alleges Otter.ai's AI note-taker recorded and transcribed a video meeting without the consent of a participant who was not an Otter user, and used captured conversations to train its AI. The company says users grant permission through its privacy policy.

The complaint alleges the recordings were used to train speech-recognition and machine-learning models, raising wiretap and privacy claims.

summary: A Delaware court found that a game publisher's CEO largely followed ChatGPT's advice in a plan to avoid paying an earnout, including removing a studio's leaders. The judge ordered the studio head reinstated, ruling he had been improperly removed.

The court tied the strategy to wrongful terminations and loss of studio control.

Reports link the chatbot use to his mental decline but not to direct instructions.
technical_summary: A general-purpose chatbot was used heavily as a companion by a user with bipolar disorder and delusions. Experts testified that this use, together with work stress, contributed to his mental instability. Reporting does not establish that the chatbot encouraged violence; the failure mode is unsafe companion-style use.
